Fix

Corrected Code

C
#include <stdio.h>

#define SIZE 9

int grid[SIZE][SIZE];

void initGrid()
{
    for(int i=0;i<SIZE;i++)
        for(int j=0;j<SIZE;j++)
            grid[i][j]=0;
}

void setValue(int row,int col,int value)
{
    grid[row][col]=value;
}

int getValue(int row,int col)
{
    return grid[row][col];
}

int isCellEmpty(int row,int col)
{
    return grid[row][col]==0;
}

int main()
{
    initGrid();
    setValue(0,0,5);

    printf("%d\n", getValue(0,0));

    return 0;
}

You said:
can i intialiaze size in main function

ChatGPT said:

Zeba, no, you cannot initialize SIZE in main() if you want to use it for:

C
int grid[SIZE][SIZE];

because array sizes must be known before main() runs.

Why?

When the program is compiled, the compiler must already know the size of grid.
But main() runs after compilation, so it's too late.

Correct ways to define SIZE

1️⃣ Using #define (most common)

C
#define SIZE 9
int grid[SIZE][SIZE];

2️⃣ Using const

C
const int SIZE = 9;
int grid[9][9];

But here the array still needs a fixed number.

3️⃣ Using dynamic memory (advanced way)

If you want the size to be decided in main(), you must use dynamic allocation:

C
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int **grid;

int main()
{
    int SIZE = 9;

    grid = malloc(SIZE * sizeof(int*));
    for(int i=0;i<SIZE;i++)
        grid[i] = malloc(SIZE * sizeof(int));

    return 0;
}

But this is not necessary for Sudoku.

✅ Best option for you

C
#define SIZE 9

It is simple and standard for Sudoku programs.

  • origin → your GitHub repository

  • main → your branch

  • -u / --set-upstream → links your local branch with GitHub

After you run this once, future pushes become simple:

git push
